lecture_summary: Circular-motion dynamics: relate angular and linear motion, distinguish radial from tangential acceleration, identify the real forces producing inward acceleration, and apply radial free-body equations to Ferris-wheel and friction-limited turntable problems.

videos.title: Rotational Motion Physics, Basic Introduction, Angular Velocity & Tangential Acceleration
videos.reason: Establishes the angular-to-linear relationships, period and frequency, and the distinction among tangential and centripetal acceleration needed for both lecture examples.

videos.title: Normal Force on a Hill, Centripetal Force, Roller Coaster Problem, Vertical Circular Motion, Physics
videos.reason: The closest match to the Ferris-wheel analysis: draw radial free-body diagrams and determine how normal force changes between the top and bottom of a vertical circle.

videos.title: Static Friction, Centripetal Force, Circular Motion, Car Rounding Curve & Rotor Ride Physics Problem
videos.reason: Covers static friction as the real inward force and the limiting-friction condition for maximum circular speed; its flat-curve calculation is mathematically equivalent to the turntable coin problem.
